findings.waiverReason: True positive, but nothing to fix: the corpus names Charybdis 17x (Apollodorus E.7.20-E.7.23, Odyssey 12, Ovid) and every mention is a sea hazard in a strait -- 'in the other cliff was Charybdis, who thrice a day drew up the water and spouted it again'. No parentage, marriage, killing, or any other relation in the existing vocabulary is attested for her anywhere in the six sources (unlike Scylla, whose parents Apollodorus does name at E.7.20, and who has 17 rows). Odysseus passes her but does not fight or kill her, and there is no 'encountered' relation; inventing one to satisfy this check would be the tail wagging the dog, and fabricating a parentage is the DEV-047/DEV-095 line this project does not cross. Revisit if P5b's myth/participant work adds a modeling shape for 'hazard encountered during a voyage'.
